topics.title: Complementary & Supplementary Angles
topics.concept:
What are Complementary Angles?

Two angles are complementary if their measures add up to 90°.

  • Each angle is called the complement of the other
  • They don't have to be adjacent (next to each other)

Example: 30° + 60° = 90° → Complementary

What are Supplementary Angles?

Two angles are supplementary if their measures add up to 180°.

  • Each angle is called the supplement of the other
  • They don't have to be adjacent

Example: 110° + 70° = 180° → Supplementary

FINDING COMPLEMENTARY ANGLE:

    If one angle is 35°, complement = 90° - 35° = 55°
    If one angle is 72°, complement = 90° - 72° = 18°


FINDING SUPPLEMENTARY ANGLE:

    If one angle is 115°, supplement = 180° - 115° = 65°
    If one angle is 45°, supplement = 180° - 45° = 135°

examples.problem: Two angles are complementary. One is 3 times the other. Find both angles.
An angle is 30° more than its supplement. Find the angle.
examples.solution:
• Let angle = x, supplement = 180° - x
  • x = (180° - x) + 30°
  • x = 210° - x
  • 2x = 210°
  • x = 105°
  • Answer: 105°

recap: Angles don't have to be adjacent

topics.title: Vertical & Adjacent Angles
topics.concept:
Vertical Angles

When two lines intersect, they form two pairs of vertical angles.

Vertical angles are ALWAYS EQUAL!

        ┌─────┐
        │     │
     ───┼─────┼───
        │     │
        └─────┘

Angle 1 = Angle 3 (vertical)
Angle 2 = Angle 4 (vertical)

Adjacent Angles on a Line

When two angles share a vertex and a side, and together form a straight line, they are adjacent and supplementary (sum to 180°).

        /  
       / 1│
      /   │
     /    │
    └─────┘
    2

Angles 1 and 2 are adjacent and form a linear pair
1 + 2 = 180°

examples.problem: Two intersecting lines form angles. One angle is 55°. Find the other three.
examples.solution:
• Vertical angle = also 55°
  • Adjacent angles = 180° - 55° = 125°
  • Other vertical angle = 125°
  • Answer: 55°, 125°, 125°

recap: Vertical angles are opposite each other
Adjacent angles on a line sum to 180°
When lines intersect, 4 angles are formed
Opposite angles are equal, adjacent are supplementary

topics.title: Angles in a Triangle Sum to 180°
topics.concept:
Triangle Angle Sum Theorem

The sum of the three interior angles in ANY triangle is always 180°!

∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

Why is this true? If you tear off the corners of a triangle and put them together, they form a straight line (180°).

Finding Missing Angles:

  • If you know two angles, subtract their sum from 180°

examples.problem: A triangle has angles 45° and 55°. Find the third angle.
A right triangle has one angle of 35°. Find the other acute angle.
examples.solution:
• Right triangle → one angle is 90°
  • Known: 90° + 35° = 125°
  • Third angle = 180° - 125° = 55°
  • Answer: 55°

examples.problem: An equilateral triangle has all angles equal. Find each angle.
A triangle has angles in ratio 2:3:4. Find each angle.
examples.solution:
• Sum of ratio parts = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9
  • 180° ÷ 9 = 20° per part
  • Angles: 40°, 60°, 80°
  • Answer: 40°, 60°, 80°

recap: Can find missing angle by subtracting from 180°
